formula_checks.name: totalAssets
formula_checks.why: The formula says every account balance is summed and missing balance counts as zero. DEC-2747f says accounts with no value must not be counted in the asset total, and DEC-3279e says a missing balance is never $0: leave it out and name the account.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum only accounts with an actual value. If an account is missing its value, omit that account from the numeric total and show an amber notice naming it; do not make the total appear complete.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-2747f and DEC-3279e; tenets 1 and 3.

formula_checks.name: cashTotal
formula_checks.why: The calculation follows the class split, but the card does not specify how a missing or invalid cash portion is represented, and its screen figure’s refusal condition (“nothing logged and no plan set”) is not directly determined by cashTotal itself. It must preserve the invariant with the other class totals.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum known cash portions only; keep missing amounts visibly unknown and disclose incompleteness rather than treating them as zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-2441; tenets 2–4.

formula_checks.name: equitiesTotal

formula_checks.name: fixedIncomeTotal

formula_checks.name: alternativesTotal
formula_checks.why: It reads the Alternatives class line from the shared class split, including only that portion of split accounts.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-2441; DEC-3035n; DEC-3146.

formula_checks.name: realEstateTotal
formula_checks.why: It reads the Real estate class line from the shared class split. The card should be checked to ensure split-account portions, rather than whole balances, are used.

formula_checks.name: investmentsTotal
formula_checks.why: The stated categories and invariant are right, but the formula does not state how missing account values are handled. The Unclassified amount is included in investments, as required by the definition, while cash and real assets are excluded.
formula_checks.should_be: Add Stocks / Funds + Bonds & CDs + Alternatives + Unclassified class portions; exclude cash and real assets; ensure cash + investments equals investableAssets for complete valued data and flag missing balances.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions 13–15 and DEC-3146; tenet 2.

formula_checks.name: investableAssets
formula_checks.why: It excludes physical assets and skips missing balances. That avoids adding unknown values as zero, but does not say how the total signals that omitted accounts make the displayed total incomplete, as required by DEC-3279e.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum known balances for non-real assets and separately identify any missing-valued accounts so the displayed total is not presented as complete.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-3279e; tenets 2 and 3.

formula_checks.name: wrapperWord
formula_checks.why: The map gives plain labels for known account kinds and returns no wrapper label for kinds that name holdings rather than account wrappers, unless the person confirmed brokerage. This follows the described distinction.

formula_checks.name: accountLastFour
formula_checks.why: The mask takes precedence over the account number. If a mask exists but contains fewer than four digits, the formula returns null rather than falling back to a valid account number; “or failing that its account number” should clarify whether failure means absent mask or unusable mask.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the mask if it yields at least four digits; otherwise try the account number; return null only when neither source has at least four digits.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card formula and ordinary fallback semantics.

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayName

rules_held.rule: DEC-1558 — On the Bonds screen a person’s bonds are listed soonest-maturing first.
rules_held.why: The governing orchestrator and Bonds screen are outside Part 1; no formula in this batch implements bond ordering.

rules_held.rule: DEC-1559 — On a holding’s page, when nothing has been sold, the Realized from sales row reads "$0 — nothing sold".
rules_held.why: Holding-detail screen and realized-gain row are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-1668 — The emergency fund counts rent from a property. Rent keeps arriving when pay stops, so each month it is added to the cash: months = cash ÷ (a month of essentials − the rent).
rules_held.why: The emergency-fund and income-summary formulas are outside Part 1; cashTotal alone cannot establish rent runway behavior.

rules_held.rule: DEC-1925 — Every property, mortgage and debt has a name the person gives it. Each mortgage is matched to a property in Net worth. A property can have no mortgage; a mortgage cannot be without a property. So there are never more mortgages than properties: three properties, three mortgages or fewer.
rules_held.why: Mortgage matching and debt minimum logic are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-1926 — A property is a second or vacation home unless rental income is entered for it on the Income screen. With rental income entered, it is a rental.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-013’s single-property branch can return a stored “rental” use when no rent entry names it, contrary to the rule that rental status requires Income-screen rent.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2334 — Private equity and hedge funds are not offered anywhere in this phase. The kinds offered are crypto, gold and commodities, annuities and other. A row saved with one of the two kinds earlier is kept as it is.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-023 preserves the wrapper-label distinction for legacy holding kinds, but whether the add-account UI blocks new private-equity/hedge-fund entries is outside this batch.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2440 — The first batch of the outside review of Net worth is closed. Everything corrected in it stands: every return time-weighted, rent counted in the emergency fund, every debt counted from Debts, a mortgage on a named property, and the smaller fixes to bonds, holdings and the account page.
rules_held.why: This broad closure covers multiple orchestrators/screens and implementation behavior not fully represented by Part 1 cards.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2441 — He read three lists for the second batch — eleven errors fixed, six places where the app was kept against the reviewer, four agreed points not yet built — and approved them all, with one change made alongside: private equity and hedge funds are not offered in this phase (DEC-2334).
rules_held.why: This closure spans formulas and screens across several batches; the Part 1 descriptions alone cannot verify every correction in the decision.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484b — The average yield of the bonds counts only bonds that have a value today, on that value as entered (refined 2026-10-09 by DEC-3390: it was the value less accrued interest). Before: an unpriced bond added its interest to the top and nothing to the bottom — three bonds read 6.09% where 4.22% is right.
rules_held.why: Bond summary average-yield behavior is MK-NW-F-061, outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484c — The if-rates-move estimate on a bond is rounded in proportion to the bond’s size, not always to the nearest $1,000. Before: a $10,000 bond read $10,000 to $10,000 whichever way rates moved.
rules_held.why: Bond rate sensitivity is MK-NW-F-064, outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484d — A sale of shares takes the oldest purchase first. Before: the gain on a sale was worked from an average cost.
rules_held.why: FIFO capital gains are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484e — A hand-built investment account shows its own uninvested cash inside it. Before: the cash it recorded was missing from the account’s own breakdown.
rules_held.why: The account orchestrator and class breakdown are outside Part 1; cashTotal consumes the shared breakdown but cannot prove its construction.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484f — A typed value is called old after six whole months have passed, counted to the day. Before: it counted month names crossed, so 30 April read six months old on 1 October.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-003 counts whole completed calendar months to the day and marks stale at six or more.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484g — Any account that already lists holdings can take a recorded buy or sale. Before: a fixed-income brokerage holding bond funds could not be chosen.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-005 allows ticker entry when holdings already exist, after the unconditional disallowed account types.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484h — A Roth 401(k) is its own choice when adding an account: a 401(k) in the Roth tax bucket. Before: the form had no Roth 401(k).
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-010 explicitly maps Roth 401(k) to kind 401(k) with Roth bucket.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484i — A maturity date makes an account Bonds & CDs before its name is read; property that is not a house is personal property. Before: a CD named ‘savings’ read as cash, and a ring could be filed as real estate.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-011 gives maturity date priority over name evidence after a stated class.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484j — A 529 is tax-free for education and an HSA is pre-tax but tax-free for medical costs, and their pages say so. Before: a 529 read ‘taxable’ and an HSA read ‘taxed when it comes out’.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-012 defaults a 529 to tax-free and an HSA/pre-tax account to tax-deferred; taxWordsOf supplies the fixed HSA/529 wording in its own card.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484k — Cash a hand-built account records for itself is on the Cash line; a holding with no price is never counted as cash. Before: that cash was in no Cash line, and an unpriced holding’s value could fall into cash.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-016 includes the hand-built account’s recorded uninvested cash through the class breakdown.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484l — Investments is one function, and Cash + Investments always equals Cash and investments together. Before: the Investments line was added up in more than one place.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-021 states the invariant cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets and excludes cash from investments.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484m — No two accounts show the same name: alike names are numbered · 1, · 2 in the order the accounts were made. Before: two accounts could read the same.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-026 makes duplicate account names unique by deterministic suffixing.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484n — A holding nobody has classed is Unclassified everywhere, and the words under an account count holdings by that same test. Before: Net worth said Unclassified and the account page said Stocks / Funds.
rules_held.why: The governing holding classifier and class label are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484o — The return on the retirement money weighs each account by the money set aside for retirement. Kept as built; the reviewer wanted a different weighting (held).
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-004 reconstructs each beginning retirement amount as current/(1+reported return) and calculates total ending / total beginning − 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484q — A money-market fund a broker flags is kept as a holding, not dropped. Before: such funds vanished at sync.
rules_held.why: Broker-sync ingestion is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2484r — The person’s own answer about a holding’s class outranks what its name suggests. Before: the name won.
rules_held.why: The rule is about holdingClassOf (MK-NW-F-109), outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746b — Only a vehicle can be the car you drive. Before: a jewellery collection worth more than the car was taken as the car.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746c — The rate the retirement money grows at, and its spread, are blended over exactly the money set aside, with no figure when nothing is set aside. Before: an invented 6% and 12% stood in.
rules_held.why: Blended return and volatility are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746d — With nothing owned there is no average return. Before: it said 7%.
rules_held.why: The build-assets-state formula is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746e — Monthly contributions: the 401(k) answer is held at the yearly legal limit for the age reached this year; property savings do not count; nothing answered gives no figure. Before: no limit, property savings counted, and $0 for nothing answered.
rules_held.why: Monthly contribution limit logic is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746f — History shared is counted in months and never rounded up to a year. Before: eighteen months read ‘2 years’.
rules_held.why: History coverage is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746g — Itemising never lowers an account’s total; whatever is not itemised stays as cash. Before: a part-itemised $186,442 could fall to $148,001.
rules_held.why: Itemization total logic is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2746h — Accounts made by itemising carry the original’s retirement share, source and wrapper; a bond’s face value is entered or left blank. Before: itemising moved money out of the nest egg and gave bonds an invented face value.
rules_held.why: Building itemized accounts is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2747c — With nothing held there is no growth figure for alternatives. Before: it showed $0 growth.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2747d — A money-market settlement fund is a fund, and a bond word inside a company name is not a bond. Before: a settlement fund read as cash; Treasury Wine Estates read as a bond.

rules_held.rule: DEC-2747e — With two or more properties and no use stated, the one entered first is the home; the others count toward retirement. Before: every such property was the home, so a second property fell out of the retirement money.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035g — Broker Treasury wording (TREAS, UST, T-bond) counts as a Treasury in the words under an account, and more than one reads Treasuries. Before: a broker’s T-bill read ‘1 bond’.
rules_held.why: Treasury wording under an account is handled by MK-NW-F-028, outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035h — A value dated by its month alone is shown as the 1st of that month. Before: the stored text was handed back unchanged.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-003 represents a month-only date as the first day of that month.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035i — Performance draws no walk for a window its record exists but cannot reach; a sentence names the record’s first day. Before: the beginning was worked back from today and wealth generated shown as if measured.
rules_held.why: The performance orchestrator is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035j — A rate the person set themselves is labelled an estimate. Before: it took the record’s flag.
rules_held.why: Benchmark info is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035k — An employer’s percent match is taken on the 401(k) figure after the yearly limit. Before: on the figure as typed — $1,600 where $1,490 is right.
rules_held.why: Contribution match logic is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035l — History shared is rounded down and its sentence built from whole months only. Before: one day short of a year read ‘1 year’.
rules_held.why: History coverage is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035m — Accounts made by itemising carry the typical rate for their class, never 0%, and a bond rate not entered stays blank. Before: every itemised account had a 0% rate.
rules_held.why: Itemized account creation is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035n — The Other investments summary reads the class split, so its total is the Alternatives line’s dollars and each part is rated by what it is. Before: whole accounts only — $18,641 where the Alternatives line read $23,031.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-002 reads each Alternatives class portion through altPartsOf, rates portions by kind, and makes total equal the Alternatives line.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035o — A property’s name is not read as evidence of its class; a fund that writes options is a fund. Before: ‘Silver Lake house’ read as an alternative and a covered-call ETF as options.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-011 explicitly excludes property/place names from name-based class evidence.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3035p — What a property is for has one reading for every function; handed the rent entries, a property is a rental only when an entry names it, and a household with no home is told so. Before: three functions read it three ways; a rented-out house marked home counted as the home.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-013’s standalone and household branches do not guarantee one shared rental/home interpretation when a stored use exists but no rent entry names the property.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3146 — Under each class heading, every account that holds money in that class is listed by its name with only its part in that class (for example Vanguard -0008 $45,000, Chase -0333 $34,000), so the rows under a heading add up to the heading. It replaces the batch 4 rule that listed a split account once, under its largest class, at its whole balance.
rules_held.why: The governing ledgerGroups and screen rows are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279b — Years to maturity are exact, by anniversaries: one year to the day is exactly 1. Before: days ÷ 365.25 (0.9993 for one year).
rules_held.why: Years-to-maturity calculation is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279c — A bond is priced at exact times, its yearly coupon on each maturity anniversary; a matured bond or one with no date has no price. Before: years rounded to a whole number, at least 1, so a matured bond still paid.
rules_held.why: Bond pricing is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279e — A missing balance is never $0: it is left out of the total and the amber box names the account. Before: a linked account that failed to sync added 0 and the total looked complete.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-015 counts missing balances as zero; MK-NW-F-022 omits missing balances without specifying the required amber warning naming the account.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279f — Itemised sums are exact decimals, a holding with no value is left out, and the remainder is then not final. Before: a missing value was 0 and the remainder looked complete; sums could leave a fraction of a cent.
rules_held.why: Itemization functions are outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279g — A kind that names contents — crypto, private equity, hedge funds, other — claims no Brokerage wrapper unless the person confirmed one. Before: ‘Coinbase Brokerage’ for a crypto wallet.
rules_held.why: MK-NW-F-023 gives no wrapper word to crypto/private-equity/hedge-fund/other kinds unless brokerage is confirmed.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279h — CDs, certificates of deposit and share certificates are recognised as CDs; ABCD Growth Fund is not. Before: ‘No-Penalty CDs’ was not a CD.
rules_held.why: CD detection is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279i — The accrued-interest note shows only for a bond that pays interest and has no accrued figure entered. Before: a zero-coupon bond got the note.
rules_held.why: Accrued-interest caveat is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3279j — Dates are read as calendar dates, never shifted by a time zone; an empty date shows nothing. Before: a midnight-UTC date could show the day before in Pacific time.
rules_held.why: Date formatting is outside Part 1.

rules_held.rule: DEC-3390 — The value typed for a bond is what the statement shows, which leaves out the interest earned since the last coupon. For the yield to maturity, that interest is added: the figure entered, or an estimate from the coupon schedule, and then the screen reads: "Added estimated $1,119 in accrued interest to bond value at 4.5% coupon for 363 days to calculate YTM. If this is not accurate, enter actual accrued interest". The yield on today's value is on the value as entered. A $25,000 4.5% Treasury worth $24,200 two days before its coupon now reads 5.69%, not 7.44%.
rules_held.why: Bond current yield, YTM, accrued interest and Bonds screen behavior are outside Part 1.
